title: Two fitted ASASSN-14ko drag orbits cannot power typical flares by direct collision heat for a one-solar-mass star
abstract: We test the energy and gas budgets of two published coupled drag fits to ASASSN-14ko. We hold the fitted disc and orbit fixed and use a one-solar-mass star with unit drag coefficient. An inelastic collision closure gives 0.69-2.44e48 erg of heat per orbit, at least 82 times below a reference flare energy of 2e50 erg. Even twice this heat supplies less than 2.5 percent of the reference energy. The gas hit in 35 orbits totals 0.051-0.053 solar masses. Its later accretion could supply the mean reference flare energy at 7.3-7.7 percent efficiency, but some individual orbits need up to 19 percent without storage. In the sampled constant-clock era the gas mass per orbit rises while collision heat falls. Ram pressure stays below 0.15 of the mean stellar pressure, so that mean-pressure test alone does not reject the fitted area. Shock durations span 0.34-6.37 stellar dynamical times. We derive mass and drag-coefficient scaling laws and a conditional heat-retention scale. This is an audit of two model fits, not new telescope evidence or proof of stellar survival. Gas transport, heat partition, changing flare fluence and stellar structure remain untested.

display.caption: Collision heat, stellar orbital work, ram pressure and shock duration for two published coupled drag fits. All curves are synthetic model outputs for a one-solar-mass star and unit drag coefficient.
Synthetic gas mass per orbit and direct collision heat. The gas budget can support a mean reference flare at about 8 percent accretion efficiency, but this does not supply rapid gas transport.
